title: Table 5: Poker - H4 (High)
description: Chain: rail-fence decode with 3 rails. Ciphertext "HOLELWRDLO".
solution_python:
def rail_fence_decode(s, rails):
    n = len(s)
    rail = [0] * n
    row, step = 0, 1
    for i in range(n):              # zigzag pattern of rails
        rail[i] = row
        if row == 0:
            step = 1
        elif row == rails - 1:
            step = -1
        row += step
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (rail[i], i))
    out = [''] * n
    for ch, pos in zip(s, order):
        out[pos] = ch
    return ''.join(out)
print(rail_fence_decode("HOLELWRDLO", 3))   # HELLOWORLD

title: Table 7: Dice - H1 (High)
description: Largest rectangle in a histogram. Monotonic stack of (start index, height). Example [2,1,5,6,2,3] gives 10.
solution_python:
def largest_rectangle(h):
    stack = []                       # (start, height), heights increasing
    best = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(h + [0]):  # sentinel 0 flushes the stack
        start = i
        while stack and stack[-1][1] >= x:
            idx, height = stack.pop()
            best = max(best, height * (i - idx))
            start = idx
        stack.append((start, x))
    return best

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S3 (Standard)
description: Return the number of 1 bits in the binary form of a non-negative integer. For a negative Python integer, count the bits of its 32-bit two's complement form.
solution_python:
def popcount(n):
    n &= 0xFFFFFFFF if n < 0 else -1
    c = 0
    while n:
        n &= n - 1
        c += 1
    return c
clues: Think about how a negative number is stored in binary.
Mask a negative value to its lowest 32 bits before counting.

Apply n AND 0xFFFFFFFF to negative values, then clear the lowest set
bit on each step until the value is zero.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S4 (Standard)
description: Return True if n is a power of two greater than 1, otherwise False. The value 1 is excluded.
solution_python:
def is_power_of_two(n):
    return n > 1 and n & (n - 1) == 0
clues: Look at how powers of two look in binary.
A power of two has exactly one set bit, and n AND (n - 1) clears that bit.
Require n to be greater than 1, then check that n AND (n - 1) is zero.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S5 (Standard)
description: Return the majority element of an array (a value that appears more than n/2 times), or None if no such value exists. Use O(1) extra space.
clues: Think about pairs of different values cancelling each other out.

A single candidate with a counter finds the only value that can survive the
cancellation.

After the pass, count how many times the candidate appears and check
that it is more than n/2.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S6 (Standard)
description: Every value appears three times except one, which appears once. Return the value that appears once. Use O(1) extra space.
clues: Consider each bit position separately.
Count the set bits at each position across all values.

Values that appear three times add 0 or 3 to each count, so count mod 3
gives the bit of the answer.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S7 (Standard)
description: Remove all occurrences of v from an array in place, keeping the order of the rest. Return how many values were removed.
clues: Consider a write index that only advances on kept values.
Copy each kept value forward while reading the array in order.

The difference between the old length and the kept count is the number of
values removed.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S8 (Standard)
description: Return the number of runs of consecutive 1 bits in the binary form of a non-negative integer. For example, 109 (1101101) has 3 runs.
clues: Look at how each bit compares with the bit before it as you scan.
A new run starts whenever a 1 follows a 0 or the start of the number.

Track the previous bit and add to the count only when the current bit is 1
and the previous bit was 0.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S9 (Standard)
description: Return the number of positions where the lowest w bits of x and y differ. Assume 1 <= w <= 31.
solution_python:
def hamming(x, y, w):
    return bin((x ^ y) & ((1 << w) - 1)).count('1')
clues: Start with the bits where x and y differ.
Only the lowest w bits matter, so mask the XOR result first.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - S10 (Standard)
description: Given a sorted array, return how many elements are strictly less than x. Use binary search.
clues: Think about the first position where the value is not less than x.

Strictly less means you stop at the first element that is equal to or greater
than x.

Use a lower-bound search: move lo past every element that is strictly less
than x, then return lo.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H1 (High)
description: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k. Values may be negative. Aim for O(n) time.
solution_python:
from collections import defaultdict
def count_subarrays_sum_k(a, k):
    seen = defaultdict(int)
    seen[0] = 1
    s = 0
    count = 0
    for x in a:
        s += x
        count += seen[s - k]
        seen[s] += 1
    return count
clues:
A subarray from i to j has sum equal to k exactly when the prefix sum up
to j minus the prefix sum up to i equals k.

For each position, you need to know how many earlier prefix sums equal
the current prefix sum minus k.

Keep a count of each prefix sum seen so far, starting with the empty
prefix 0. At each element, add the count for (current prefix sum - k) to the answer, then record the current prefix sum.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H2 (High)
description: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers that appears in an unsorted array, in O(n) expected time.
clues:
Consider how to avoid restarting counts from every number in the middle
of a run.

If you only start counting at numbers whose predecessor is missing, each
run is counted exactly once.

Put all values in a hash set. For each value whose predecessor is not in
the set, count upward while the next value is present.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H3 (High)
description: Return how much water is trapped between bars of given heights after rain. Use O(1) extra space with two pointers.
clues: Water above a bar depends on the tallest bar on its left and on its right.

The side with the smaller current height is limited by its own running
maximum, so its water can be decided without knowing the other side.

Use two pointers and two running maxima. Always advance the pointer
on the lower side, and add the running maximum minus the current height to the total.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H4 (High)
description: Given an array, return an array where each position holds the product of all other elements, without using division. Zeros may appear.
solution_python:
def product_except_self(a):
    n = len(a)
    out = [1] * n
    prefix = 1
    for i in range(n):
        out[i] = prefix
        prefix *= a[i]
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= a[i]
    return out
clues: Each output value combines what is to its left with what is to its right.

Two passes can compute the left product and the right product
separately, and no division is needed.
First pass: store the product of everything to the left of each index.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H5 (High)
description: Return True if some three distinct indices of the array have values that sum to zero. Use O(n^2) time.
clues: Fix one value and look for two others that complete it to zero.

After sorting, the two remaining values can be found with two pointers,
moving one of them depending on the sign of the partial sum.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H6 (High)
description: Given start and end times of meetings (equal-length lists), return the minimum number of rooms needed so no two overlapping meetings share a room.
solution_python:
def min_rooms(starts, ends):
    s = sorted(starts)
    e = sorted(ends)
    rooms = best = 0
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] < e[j]:
            rooms += 1
            best = max(best, rooms)
            i += 1
        else:
            rooms -= 1
            j += 1
    return best
clues: Count how many meetings are active at the moment each meeting starts.

Sorting starts and ends separately lets you sweep through time and track
the number of active meetings.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H7 (High)

clues:
Palindromes grow outward from a center, which can be a character or a

For each possible center, expanding outward while the characters match

Try every center, both single-character centers and gaps between

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H8 (High)
description: Count the islands in a grid of "1" (land) and "0" (water). Islands are groups of land cells connected horizontally or vertically.

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H9 (High)
description: Return the k-th largest element of an array (k is 1-based). Duplicates count separately.
clues:
Think about which elements you need to keep around to answer the
question.

You do not need a full ordering. Keeping a small structure of the k largest

Maintain a min-heap of size k. Push each value, pop when the heap

title: Table 9: Coin Flip - H10 (High)
description: Given an array where each value is the maximum jump length from that position, return the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index. Assume the last index is reachable.
clues:
Think of the positions reachable with exactly one jump, then with two, and
so on.

Each jump covers a window of positions, and the next jump should start
from the farthest point you can reach inside the current window.

Track the end of the current window and the farthest index reachable so
far. Each time you reach the end of the window, count one jump and extend the window to the farthest index.

title: Table 10: The Vault - S5 (Standard)
description: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head and the number of nodes as a pair.
solution_python:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev = None
    count = 0
    while head:
        head.next, prev, head = prev, head, head.next
        count += 1
    return prev, count
